name: obol_flag_hunt_2026_09
description: Thorough post-foothold flag capture. Reads well-known flag files through the existing SSH/WinRM proof channel, prints each flag next to a host-identity command (for the exam screenshot), and records what it actually reads.

source.name: O.B.O.L flag capture methodology
source.notes: Runs a single non-interactive recursive search per OS over an existing proven foothold; a captured flag is proof, not a checkbox. Each flag is printed with its own identity block so one screenshot per flag satisfies OffSec's flag+ipconfig requirement.

actions.title: Hunt for flags (Linux)
actions.hypothesis: A Linux foothold should be able to read the engagement flag files; capturing their contents proves the objective.

report.finding: Captured a flag file from the Linux foothold.

commands.note: STEP 1 — LOCATE (from your box). Find every flag file so you know its path before you log in. This is a one-liner from Kali, so it only LOCATES — OffSec scores a flag read this way ZERO. Paste the output back and obol records each flag's path; capture it on the host in steps 3-4.
STEP 2 — GET ON THE HOST (interactive). Open a real shell on the target; the report proof must be a screenshot of THIS session. Run steps 3-4 inside it.

STEP 3 — ON THE HOST, capture the LOCAL/user flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE the step-2 shell and screenshot the whole frame: id + ip addr (the target IP) + the flag, together. The path fills from what step 1 located; adjust it if you skipped the locate. obol records this as the captured local flag.
commands.run: id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_local}}

commands.note: STEP 4 — ON THE HOST, capture the ROOT flag with its identity (after you escalate to root). Run this INSIDE a root shell and screenshot the whole frame together. obol records this as the captured root flag.
commands.run: id; hostname; ip -4 addr | grep inet; cat {{flag_path_root}}

actions.title: Hunt for flags (Windows)
actions.hypothesis: A Windows foothold should be able to read the engagement flag files; capturing their contents proves the objective, and printing each next to ipconfig gives the exam screenshot.

report.finding: Captured a flag file from the Windows foothold.

commands.note: STEP 1 — LOCATE (from your box). Spider C$ for the flag files so you know each one's exact path (which user's Desktop) before you log in. This runs from Kali, so it only LOCATES the flags — OffSec scores a flag read this way ZERO. Paste the output back and obol records each flag's path and fills it into steps 3-4; you capture it on the host there.

STEP 2 — GET ON THE HOST (interactive). Log in with the dumped hash — no plaintext needed. The report proof must be a screenshot of THIS session (a shell on the target), so run steps 3-4 inside it. For a SYSTEM shell instead, use impacket-psexec {{domain}}/{{user}}@{{target}} -hashes :{{nthash}}.

STEP 3 — ON THE HOST, capture the LOCAL flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE the step-2 session and screenshot the whole frame: hostname + ipconfig (the target IP) + the flag, together. The path fills from what step 1 located (the right user's Desktop, the platform's own flag name); adjust it if you skipped the locate. obol records this as the captured local flag.

STEP 4 — ON THE HOST, capture the ROOT/proof flag with its identity. Run this INSIDE the step-2 session (or a SYSTEM/Administrator shell) and screenshot the whole frame together. The path fills from what step 1 located. obol records this as the captured root flag.
